findings.title: ContextualLoggerMiddleware panics on nil requests
findings.body: QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth and CollectMetrics dereference req (e.g. req.PluginContext) without a nil check. LoggerMiddleware in the same package explicitly guards `if req == nil`, showing nil requests are expected. A nil request through this middleware causes a nil-pointer panic instead of delegating to next.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext discards logged output
findings.body: TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand new TestLogger instead of itself or a logger sharing storage. LoggerMiddleware now does `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, so when tests inject a TestLogger the Info/Warn/Error counts go to the discarded instance. Assertions on the original InfoLogs/WarnLogs/ErrorLogs will always see zero calls, breaking test observability and diverging from the real wrapper which preserves the underlying logger.

findings.title: MetricsMiddleware shares mutable instance across clients
findings.body: NewMetricsMiddleware creates one *MetricsMiddleware and on each decoration does `imw.next = next; return imw`. The same struct is reused for every plugin client, mutating `next` without synchronization. Concurrent decoration or multiple clients causes data races and requests routed to the wrong `next` client. ContextualLoggerMiddleware in the same PR correctly creates a new struct per decoration.

findings.title: Adding FromContext breaks Logger interface implementers
findings.body: The Logger interface gains a new required method `FromContext(context.Context) Logger`. Any out-of-tree implementation of the old 5-method interface no longer compiles. This is a breaking API change made without a fallback, adapter, or major-version note, while only the in-tree wrapper and test fake were updated.

findings.title: LoggerMiddleware drops traceID from request logs
findings.body: The old logRequest explicitly added `traceID` from `tracing.TraceIDFromContext` plus pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname. The new version only logs status/duration/eventName and relies on `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)`. The context enrichment in instrumentContext only adds endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname and never adds traceID, so Plugin Request Completed logs lose trace correlation unless the underlying logger injects it, which the removed code did not rely on.
